subject: Emotions
title: Creativity and Melancholy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Creativity and Melancholy.

hook.text: Beethoven wrote his best work while going deaf. Frida Kahlo painted her pain. Sadness fuels creation.

buildup.text: Aristotle asked: 'Why are all men of genius melancholic?' The link between sadness and art is ancient.

discovery.text: Modupe Akinola found that negative feedback boosted creative output. Mild sadness sharpens artistic thinking.

twist.text: The effect has limits. Severe depression kills creativity. The sweet spot is mild melancholy, not anguish.

climax.text: Sad art resonates because it's honest. Audiences recognize truth in vulnerability they rarely see.

punchline.text: The best art comes from the worst feelings.

quiz.question: What did Akinola find about negative feedback?
